name: Antigua and Barbuda
summary: Antigua and Barbuda publishes no procedure for bringing a casket in. The Public Health Act (Cap. 353) lets the Central Board of Health regulate embalming, preservation and transport of corpses, but no import permit or checklist is published online: work through a licensed Antiguan funeral home, which confirms clearance with the health authorities and Customs before departure.
documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death, with English translation (expected; not officially published)
Embalming certificate (expected; not officially published)
Removal or export permit from the country of death
Non-contagious disease certificate (commonly requested; confirm)
Passport of the deceased
Name of the receiving Antiguan funeral home
coffin: No Antiguan import standard is published. A hermetically sealed (zinc or metal lined) casket in an outer case meets airline rules and is the safe choice; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
embalming: Public Health Act Cap. 353, s.160, empowers the Central Board of Health to make regulations on embalming, preservation and transport of corpses from Antigua and Barbuda; no regulation for incoming bodies was found online. Embalming is expected in practice and is required for bodies leaving the country (gov.uk).
consular: No Antiguan consular procedure for incoming remains is published. Ask the Antigua and Barbuda High Commission or consulate in the country of death whether documents must be authenticated.
arrival: Not published officially. The receiving funeral home normally arranges customs and health clearance at V. C. Bird International Airport. All major funeral directors have cold storage (the main hospital has none). There are no cremation facilities in Antigua or Barbuda; cremation is arranged abroad (Puerto Rico, Barbados or Grenada).
private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo; the documents travel with the coffin and are presented to customs and health officials at the arrival airport. The coffin (typically about 2.2 m long, 70-100 kg once zinc-lined) must physically fit the aircraft's cargo door or a cabin configured for it, which rules out many light and midsize jets. Land at V. C. Bird International Airport (St John's) with customs clearance arranged and have the receiving funeral home meet the aircraft. No specific rule for private flights carrying remains was found.
private_jet_note: Confirm entry documents with the local funeral home before take-off.
export: The death is registered with the Civil Registry by the next of kin or a funeral director with a letter of authorisation; the certificate is issued in English within a few days and states the cause of death. Post-mortems are carried out by forensic doctors appointed by the hospital or court and their timing depends on the police investigation, which can delay release. Local funeral directors provide the death certificate, a certificate of embalming and a certificate giving permission to transfer the remains. Infectious conditions must be reported to the local authorities.
export_points: Civil Registry death certificate in English, with cause of death
Embalming certificate and permission to transfer required
Police-led post-mortem timing can delay release
No crematorium; cremation is arranged abroad

at_a_glance.consular: Ask an Antigua and Barbuda mission
at_a_glance.permit: Not published; confirm with funeral home

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving Antiguan funeral home.
Antiguan funeral home confirms entry documents with health and Customs.
Obtain death certificate, embalming, sealed casket and export permit.
Check with the mission whether documents need authentication.
Customs and health clearance at V. C. Bird; funeral home collects.

key_points: Entry rules are not published online
Public Health Act lets the Central Board of Health regulate transport of corpses
No cremation facilities in the country
authority: Central Board of Health / Ministry of Health; Civil Registry; Customs (entry procedure not published)

name: Anguilla
summary: Anguilla is a UK Overseas Territory with its own laws; UK rules do not apply. No procedure for bringing a casket into Anguilla is published; a 2010 Cadaver (Importation) Bill concerns only cadavers for medical research. Work through an Anguilla funeral home and confirm clearance with the Health Authority and Customs before departure.
documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death, with English translation (expected; not officially published)
Embalming certificate (expected; not officially published)
Removal or export permit from the country of death
Non-contagious disease certificate (commonly requested; confirm)
Passport of the deceased
Name of the receiving Anguilla funeral home
coffin: No Anguilla import standard is published. A hermetically sealed (zinc or metal lined) casket in an outer case meets airline rules; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
embalming: Not published officially; embalming is expected for international transport.
consular: Anguilla has no consulates of its own; UK missions handle consular matters for Anguillians abroad. No legalisation requirement was found; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
arrival: Not published officially. The receiving funeral home normally arranges customs and health clearance and the local burial formalities.
private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo; the documents travel with the coffin and are presented to customs and health officials at the arrival airport. The coffin (typically about 2.2 m long, 70-100 kg once zinc-lined) must physically fit the aircraft's cargo door or a cabin configured for it, which rules out many light and midsize jets. Land at Clayton J. Lloyd International Airport, the territory's port of entry, with customs clearance arranged; its runway limits larger jets. No specific rule for private flights carrying remains was found.
private_jet_note: Confirm documents with the local health authority and aircraft suitability before take-off.
export: Not published online. A local funeral home normally registers the death, obtains the death certificate and any removal permit, and arranges embalming and sealing to meet the destination's rules.
export_points: Death registered with the local civil registry
Local removal permit and embalming expected
Destination country's requirements apply
Not published officially; confirm locally

Anguilla funeral home confirms entry clearance with Health and Customs.
Obtain death certificate, embalming, sealed casket and export permit.

name: Barbados
summary: Barbados publishes no procedure for bringing a casket in. A Barbados funeral home must receive the casket and handle health and customs clearance; expect embalming, a sealed casket and a death certificate with cause of death, and confirm with a Barbados mission (the Toronto consulate advises on transporting deceased persons to Barbados).
documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death (expected; not officially published)
Certificate of cause of death / non-contagious disease certificate (expected; not officially published)
Embalming certificate (expected; not officially published)
Transit / removal permit from the place of death
Confirm the list with the Barbados High Commission or consulate
coffin: Not published for entry. A hermetically sealed casket in an outer case is the regional norm and is required by most airlines. On exit, a Ministry of Health inspector checks that the body has been prepared correctly.
embalming: Not published for entry; expected in practice. On exit, the funeral director embalms after the death certificate is issued.
consular: No official consular checklist was found. The Consulate General in Toronto lists advice on transporting deceased persons to Barbados for burial as a service; contact the Barbados mission in the country of death. Barbados is often a transit point for remains bound for neighbouring islands.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at Grantley Adams International Airport; the local funeral director collects. No official burial deadline found. Barbados has one crematorium.
private_aviation: No private-flight rules found. Grantley Adams International is the port of entry; arrange customs and health clearance and the funeral home's airside collection in advance.
export: The death is registered at the Registration Department or a Magistrate's Court. Post-mortems are usual for foreign nationals, normally within 48 hours; the death certificate (English, without cause of death) usually follows within 3 days. The funeral director embalms; a Ministry of Health health inspector checks the preparation, and the Ministry issues a transit permit and a letter confirming no communicable disease. The funeral director also provides the certificate of embalming.
export_points: Post-mortem usual for foreigners, normally within 48 hours
Death certificate within about 3 days, no cause of death shown
Ministry of Health inspection, transit permit and no-communicable-disease letter
Embalming certificate from the funeral director

steps.what: Appoint funeral homes at departure and in Barbados.
Obtain death certificate, non-contagious disease certificate and embalming.
Seal the casket; confirm requirements with the Barbados mission.
Receiving funeral home confirms clearance arrangements.
Customs and health clearance; funeral home collects.

key_points: Entry rules not published online
Exit needs a Ministry of Health transit permit after inspection
Barbados certificates do not state the cause of death
Common transit point for nearby islands
authority: Ministry of Health and Wellness; Barbados Revenue Authority (Customs)

name: Bermuda
summary: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory with its own health and registration laws; UK rules do not apply. No official procedure for bringing a body into Bermuda is published: the Public Health Act 1949 covers burials and allows regulations on how remains are coffined, but no import permit was found. Plan on a death certificate, embalming certificate and sealed coffin, and confirm with a Bermuda funeral home and the Ministry of Health before shipping.
documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death, with English translation (expected; not confirmed officially)
Embalming certificate (expected; not confirmed officially)
Export or transit permit from the country of death
Any Bermuda entry permit: not published; confirm with the receiving funeral home
coffin: Not published officially. The Public Health Act 1949 (s.132) allows regulations prescribing how human remains are treated and coffined before disposal; no import rule was found. A hermetically sealed coffin with outer case is the safe standard.
embalming: Not published officially; embalming is normally expected for international transport.
consular: Bermuda has no consulates of its own abroad; UK missions handle consular matters for Bermudians. No legalisation requirement was found; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
arrival: The receiving Bermuda funeral home normally handles customs and health clearance at L.F. Wade International Airport and burial arrangements. Under the Quarantine (Maritime and Air) Regulations 2017, a death reported on board an arriving aircraft triggers port health controls; this concerns deaths in flight, not repatriated remains. Confirm timing locally.
private_aviation: Private flights arrive at L.F. Wade International Airport, the only airport, where customs and immigration clear the aircraft. Specific rules for human remains on private aircraft were not found; arrange clearance of the coffin in advance through a local funeral home and handling agent.
private_jet_note: Confirm in advance with a Bermuda funeral home that the coffin can be cleared on arrival.
export: Leaving Bermuda, the death is first registered with the Registry General on notice from a doctor or coroner; the funeral home then obtains the death certificate, embalming and any removal permit and meets the destination's requirements. No official page on export permits was found.
export_points: Death notified to the Registry General by doctor or coroner
Death certificate ordered from the Registry General
Removal permit details not published; ask the funeral home

at_a_glance.permit: Not published; confirm with funeral home

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving Bermuda funeral home.
Ask the Bermuda funeral home to confirm the entry documents and any health permit.
Obtain the death certificate, embalming and sealed coffin, and the export permit of the country of death.
Book the flight to L.F. Wade International Airport.
Customs and health clearance; funeral home collects the coffin.

key_points: Bermuda has its own laws; UK rules do not apply directly.
No official entry checklist or import permit published.
Single airport: L.F. Wade International.
authority: Government of Bermuda, Ministry of Health; Registry General

name: Dominica
summary: No official published procedure for bringing a casket into Dominica was found. Work through a Dominica funeral home, which deals with the Ministry of Health (Environmental Health) and Customs, and expect embalming and a sealed casket with a full set of departure documents.
documents: Death certificate - expected, not confirmed
Certificate of cause of death / non-contagious disease certificate - expected, not confirmed
Embalming certificate - expected, not confirmed
Transit / removal permit from the place of death - expected, not confirmed
Confirm the list with a Dominica consulate or the Ministry of Health
coffin: Not published. A hermetically sealed casket in an outer case is standard in the region and required by most airlines; confirm locally.
embalming: Not published for entry; embalming is expected in practice.
consular: No official consular procedure was found online. Ask the Dominica High Commission or consulate in the country of death whether documents must be authenticated.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at the port of entry (Douglas-Charles Airport); the local funeral home collects. No official burial deadline found. Dominica has no crematorium; scattering ashes needs permission from local authorities and the Environmental Health Department.
private_aviation: No private-flight rules were found. Use an airport of entry with customs (Douglas-Charles Airport) and arrange for the funeral home to meet the aircraft; confirm entry clearance before take-off.
export: The death is registered with the births, marriages and deaths section of the Registry Department (EC$20 per certificate copy), using the hospital's Medical Certificate of Death if there is no post-mortem. A post-mortem is usually carried out in all cases, typically within four days. If no death certificate can be issued (for example during a police investigation), the police issue a permissive warrant allowing repatriation. The local funeral director provides the certificate of embalming and a certificate giving permission to transfer the remains. There is no crematorium: cremation requires transfer to Barbados or Saint Lucia.
export_points: Death registered at the Registry Department (EC$20 per copy)
Post-mortem usual, normally within about 4 days
Police permissive warrant if no death certificate yet
No crematorium on the island

at_a_glance.permit: Not published; confirm with Ministry of Health
at_a_glance.arrival: Customs clearance; local funeral home collects

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home at departure and one in Dominica
Obtain death certificate, non-contagious disease certificate and embalming
Seal the casket; ask the Dominica consulate whether documents need authentication
Receiving funeral home confirms clearance with Health and Customs
Customs clearance; funeral home collects

key_points: Entry rules not published online
Post-mortem usual for all deaths in Dominica
No crematorium in Dominica
authority: Ministry of Health (Environmental Health Department); Customs

name: Cayman Islands
summary: Bringing a body into the Cayman Islands needs an approval letter from the Department of Environmental Health (DEH): send the Importation of Human Remains Request Form with the death certificate (cause of death, communicable or not), burial transit permit and letter of non-communicable disease at least 48 hours before arrival, and present the approval to Customs. The receiving funeral home then issues the burial order.
documents: DEH Importation of Human Remains Request Form
Death certificate stating the cause of death and whether it was communicable or non-communicable
Burial transit permit (for a body)
Letter of non-communicable disease (for a body)
Translated copies of any document not in English
Administrative fee: CI$25 / US$31.25 locally, or a US$100 bank draft from overseas, payable to CIG-DEH
coffin: DEH does not publish a casket standard for imported bodies (ashes must travel in a sealed urn or approved container). A hermetically sealed coffin with outer case meets airline rules; burial in Cayman is only in purpose-built vaults in designated cemeteries.
embalming: Not specified by DEH; embalming is normally expected for international transport. Confirm with the receiving funeral home.
consular: The Cayman Islands have no consulates of their own; UK missions handle consular matters. No legalisation is required by DEH, but documents not in English must be translated.
arrival: Present the DEH approval letter to Customs when the remains arrive. For a body brought in for burial, the funeral home issues the burial order; nothing is required from the General Registry. Any disposition needs a burial order. Public cemetery vaults: CI$1,200 adult, CI$600 child (DEH).
private_aviation: Private flights clear customs and immigration at Owen Roberts International Airport (Grand Cayman) or Charles Kirkconnell International Airport (Cayman Brac). The DEH approval letter must be in hand and shown to Customs on arrival; no other private-flight rule was found.
private_jet_note: DEH approval letter needed before arrival; apply at least 48 hours ahead.
export: Leaving the Cayman Islands, the funeral home obtains the registered death certificate, embalming and any removal documents and meets the destination's requirements. No official page on export permits was found.
export_points: Registered death certificate
Embalming and sealed coffin
Export permit details not published; ask the funeral home

at_a_glance.arrival: Show approval to Customs; funeral home collects

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving Cayman funeral home.
Gather death certificate, burial transit permit and non-communicable disease letter.
Send the DEH request form, documents and fee to dehcustomerservice@gov.ky.
Receive the DEH approval letter by email or post.
Show the approval to Customs; funeral home collects and issues the burial order.

key_points: DEH approval required at least 48 hours before arrival
Overseas fee US$100 by bank draft; local CI$25
Burial only in vaults in designated cemeteries
Funeral home issues the burial order
authority: Department of Environmental Health (DEH), Cayman Islands Government; Customs and Border Control

name: Montserrat
summary: Under the Cadavers (Importation) Act (Cap. 14.13), no body may be brought into Montserrat without a written cadaver import permit from the Chief Medical Officer, who must first be satisfied, on documents from the place of death, that export is lawful, of the cause of death and that there is no health risk. Customs must refuse landing without the permit; the fee is $1,000 per body.
documents: Cadaver import permit issued by the Chief Medical Officer (apply before shipping)
Documentary evidence from the place of death that export of the body is lawfully authorised
Evidence of the cause of death (death certificate)
Evidence that the body poses no disease risk (non-communicable disease certificate)
Consent of executors or relatives where practicable
Permit fee: $1,000 per body (Cadavers (Importation) (Fees) Regulations 2013)
coffin: The Chief Medical Officer sets the container type as a permit condition. The Act defines an impervious container as one hermetically sealed by gasket or soldered/welded metal, or a heat- or adhesive-sealed inner container inside an outer box. Customs may not open an impervious container without the Chief Medical Officer's approval. The definition also covers a heat- or adhesive-sealed plastic container inside an outer box, so a sealed pouch in a case may be acceptable if the permit allows it; confirm with the Chief Medical Officer.
embalming: Not set by the Act; embalming is expected in practice and may be imposed as a permit condition. Confirm with the Chief Medical Officer.
consular: Montserrat has no consulates of its own; UK missions handle consular matters. No legalisation requirement is set by the Act, but the export authorisation and cause of death must be documented by the place of death.
arrival: Customs at the port of entry checks the permit and may examine the container (not an impervious one without the Chief Medical Officer's approval). The permit fixes where the body is kept and how it is disposed of; burial still needs the registration formalities under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act. No customs duty is payable on the body.
private_aviation: Montserrat's only airport (John A. Osborne) has a very short runway served by small turboprops; most business jets cannot land there, so a casket often travels by small aircraft or ferry via Antigua. Without a valid cadaver import permit the aircraft or vessel will be refused permission to land the body.
private_jet_note: Cadaver import permit needed before arrival; most jets cannot land, plan a transfer via Antigua.
export: No official procedure for sending a body out of Montserrat was found. In practice the local funeral home obtains the death registration, embalming and a removal/transit permit; the Ministry of Health and Social Services should be consulted. The UK requirements for arrival in the UK apply on the receiving side.
export_points: Procedure not published; confirm with the Ministry of Health and Social Services
Local funeral home arranges registration, embalming and transit papers
Transfer usually via Antigua because of the small airport

at_a_glance.embalming: Expected; may be a permit condition
at_a_glance.arrival: Customs checks permit; funeral home collects

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and one in Montserrat.
Gather death certificate, cause of death, export authorisation and family consent.
Apply to the Chief Medical Officer for the cadaver import permit; pay $1,000.
Seal the casket as the permit requires; book transfer via Antigua if needed.
Customs checks the permit; funeral home collects for burial.

key_points: Import permit from the Chief Medical Officer is mandatory by law
Fee $1,000 per body; no customs duty
Landing refused without a permit
Airport only takes small aircraft
authority: Chief Medical Officer, Ministry of Health and Social Services, Government of Montserrat; Customs

name: Turks and Caicos Islands
summary: The Turks and Caicos Islands are a British Overseas Territory with their own health legislation; UK rules do not apply. The Environmental Health Department (port health, cemetery management) has no published guidance on importing human remains; its pages are under construction. Plan on a death certificate, embalming certificate and sealed coffin, and confirm with a local funeral home and ehd@gov.tc before shipping.
documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death, with English translation (expected; not confirmed officially)
Embalming certificate (expected; not confirmed officially)
Export or transit permit from the country of death
Any local health clearance: not published; confirm with the Environmental Health Department
coffin: Not published officially. A hermetically sealed coffin with outer case is the safe standard; confirm locally.
embalming: Not published officially; embalming is normally expected for international transport.
consular: The Turks and Caicos Islands have no consulates of their own; UK missions handle consular matters. No legalisation requirement was found.
arrival: The receiving funeral home normally handles customs and health clearance and burial arrangements. The Environmental Health Department (Butterfield Square, Providenciales; (649) 338-2143/2144; ehd@gov.tc) oversees port health and cemetery management. Confirm timing locally.
private_aviation: Private flights clear customs and immigration at an airport of entry such as Providenciales International. No specific rule for human remains on private aircraft was found; arrange clearance in advance through a local funeral home.
private_jet_note: Confirm with a local funeral home and Environmental Health that the coffin can be cleared on arrival.
export: No official page on export permits was found. The funeral home obtains the death certificate, embalming and any removal permit and meets the destination's requirements.

Embalming and sealed coffin
Removal permit details not published; ask the funeral home

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving funeral home in the Turks and Caicos.
Confirm entry documents and any health clearance with the local funeral home or Environmental Health.
Obtain the death certificate, embalming, sealed coffin and export permit of the country of death.
Book the flight to Providenciales or another airport of entry.
Customs and health clearance; funeral home collects.

key_points: The territory has its own laws; UK rules do not apply directly.
No official entry checklist was found; confirm locally.

name: British Virgin Islands
summary: To bring a body into the British Virgin Islands, submit the Application for Burial (importation and exportation of body) form to the Ministry of Health and Social Development with an authentic death certificate showing the cause of death and a burial permit from the Civil Registry; an approval letter and Importation Certificate (or a refusal) follows within two working days. There is no fee.
documents: Application for Burial / importation and exportation of body form (Ministry of Health and Social Development)
Authentic death certificate stating the cause of death (or cremation certificate for ashes)
Burial permit from the BVI Civil Registry
Embalming certificate and removal permit of the country of death (expected by airlines; not listed by the Ministry)
Ministry letter of approval and Importation Certificate (issued within two working days)
coffin: Not specified by the Ministry. A hermetically sealed coffin with outer case meets airline rules; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
embalming: Not specified by the Ministry; embalming is expected for international transport.
consular: The BVI have no consulates of their own; UK missions handle consular matters. No legalisation requirement is published; the death certificate must be authentic and state the cause of death.
arrival: Present the Ministry's letter of approval and Importation Certificate on arrival; the receiving funeral home arranges customs clearance and burial under the Civil Registry burial permit.
private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo; the documents travel with the coffin and are presented to customs and health officials at the arrival airport. The coffin (typically about 2.2 m long, 70-100 kg once zinc-lined) must physically fit the aircraft's cargo door or a cabin configured for it, which rules out many light and midsize jets. Land at Terrance B. Lettsome International Airport (Beef Island) with customs clearance arranged and the Importation Certificate in hand; have the funeral home meet the aircraft. No specific rule for private flights carrying remains was found.
private_jet_note: Get the Ministry of Health Importation Certificate before take-off (two working days).
export: Leaving the BVI: submit the same burial application form in person or by email to the Ministry of Health and Social Development with the death certificate (stating the cause of death) and/or cremation certificate; an exportation schedule and permission letter are issued, to be collected within two days. No fee.
export_points: Ministry of Health permission letter, about two days, free
Death certificate must state the cause of death
Embalming and sealing to meet destination rules
Ministry: ministryofhealth@gov.vg, +1 284 468 2272

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving BVI funeral home.
Obtain the death certificate with cause of death and a Civil Registry burial permit.
Submit the burial application form to the Ministry of Health in person or by email.
Receive the approval letter and Importation Certificate.
Present the certificate; customs clearance; funeral home collects.

key_points: Ministry of Health Importation Certificate required
Decision within two working days; no fee
Civil Registry burial permit needed in advance
authority: Ministry of Health and Social Development, Government of the Virgin Islands; Civil Registry

name: Sint Maarten
summary: Sint Maarten inherited the Netherlands Antilles burial rules: the 1975 decree implementing article 40 of the Begrafenisverordening (P.B. 1975, no. 46) allows a body to be brought in only if it is embalmed or otherwise preserved, in a hermetically sealed, absorbent-lined impervious coffin packed in an outer case, labelled, and accompanied by a medical certificate (cause of death), an embalming statement and a transport statement from the authority of the place of death. Its current Sint Maarten text is not published online; confirm with the Civil Registry and Collective Prevention Services.
documents: Medical certificate of death or death-certificate extract stating name, birth, date and place of death and cause of death (or that it was natural / non-contagious; if contagious, the disease)
Statement from the embalmer describing the embalming or preservation method
Statement from the competent authority of the place of death on the manner and route of transport
Burial permit from the Sint Maarten civil registrar (issued free on presentation of the death certificate)
coffin: Under the Antillean decree the coffin must be of impervious material, hermetically sealed and lined with absorbent material, containing only the body, clothing, packing and personal effects, and properly packed in a tight outer case to the satisfaction of the government-designated doctor. The coffin must be clearly marked with name, first names, date of birth, date and place of death and destination.
embalming: Required: the body must be embalmed or otherwise properly preserved. For a death from a quarantinable disease, arterial and cavity embalming is mandatory.
consular: Sint Maarten is a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; the Kingdom's Strasbourg Agreement ratification was declared for the Netherlands only, so a Strasbourg laissez-passer cannot be assumed to replace the documents above. No legalisation rule is published; check with the Civil Registry.
arrival: The documents are presented on arrival. Bodies brought in must be buried as soon as possible, and no burial may take place without written permission of the civil registrar naming the burial place. Overland transport between the French and Dutch sides of the island is exempt under the Antillean rules. Civil Registry: +1 721 542 0349.
private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo; the documents travel with the coffin and are presented to customs and health officials at the arrival airport. The coffin (typically about 2.2 m long, 70-100 kg once zinc-lined) must physically fit the aircraft's cargo door or a cabin configured for it, which rules out many light and midsize jets. Land at Princess Juliana International Airport with customs clearance arranged and have the receiving funeral home meet the aircraft. No specific rule for private flights carrying remains was found.
private_jet_note: Carry the original medical, embalming and transport statements with the coffin.
export: Under the same decree, a body leaving Sint Maarten must be embalmed, in a sealed impervious coffin in an outer case, labelled, with the medical certificate, embalming statement and transport statement handed over for the destination's authorities. The Civil Registry registers the death; a local funeral home arranges the rest.
export_points: Death registered with the Civil Registry
Embalming and sealed impervious coffin required
Medical, embalming and transport statements travel with the body
Destination country's rules also apply

at_a_glance.permit: Transport statement from place of death
at_a_glance.arrival: Civil registrar burial permit; bury promptly

steps.what: Appoint a funeral home abroad and a receiving Sint Maarten funeral home.
Obtain medical certificate with cause of death; embalm and get the embalmer's statement.
Seal and label the coffin; get the transport statement from the local authority.
Funeral home confirms requirements with the Civil Registry.
Present documents; civil registrar issues the burial permit; burial follows promptly.

key_points: Antillean decree requires embalming and a hermetically sealed coffin
Coffin must be labelled with identity and destination
Sint Maarten text not published online; Curacao's identical text cited
authority: Civil Registry (burial permit); Ministry of Public Health, Social Development and Labour; Customs
